codex_why: The Hebrew explicitly calls Jair בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁה, son of Manasseh, while the existing descendant-of row records only broader ancestry.
judge_why: 1KI 4:13 'Jair ben-Manasseh' uses ben for a descendant (Jair is of Segub/Hezron, 1CH 2:21-22); the site already records jair descendant-of manasseh.

codex_why: The Hebrew identifies Barachel as 'the Buzite' but does not establish descent from the particular Buz who was Nahor's son.
judge_why: JOB 32:2 gives only the gentilic 'the Buzite' (הבוזי), not a genealogy, and it may describe Elihu rather than Barachel. Which Buz is meant (Nahor's son or the Gadite of 1CH 5:14) is not stated.

codex_why: The Greek οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ names James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas as Jesus' brothers but does not specify their relationships to one another.
judge_why: MAT 13:55 names James, Joseph (Ἰωσήφ), Simon and Judas together as οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ, Jesus' brothers, so Joseph and Simon are brothers to each other.

codex_why: The Hebrew calls Jashobeam ben-Hachmoni, explicitly stating sonship beyond the recorded ancestor relationship.
judge_why: 1CH 11:11 'Jashobeam ben-Hachmoni' gives a clan name (2SA 23:8 'the Tachmonite'; 1CH 27:2 calls him son of Zabdiel). The site already records hachmoni ancestor-of joshebbasshebeth.

codex_why: The Hebrew says Ithra went in to Abigail but does not state that he was her husband.
judge_why: 2SA 17:25: Ithra 'went in to' (בא אל) Abigail and fathered Amasa by her (cf. 1CH 2:17), which supports the union recorded.

codex_why: The Hebrew names Mahalath as the wife Rehoboam took, with Abihail belonging to Mahalath's parentage rather than explicitly being another wife.
judge_why: 2CH 11:18 has no 'and' before Abihail (MT מחלת בן־ירימות ... אביהיל בת־אליאב), and 11:19 'she bare him' is singular. So Abihail may be Mahalath's mother rather than a second wife; KJV supplies 'and'.

codex_why: The Hebrew calls Malchijah בֶן־הַמֶּלֶךְ, 'son of the king,' with Zedekiah identified as the king in verse 5.
judge_why: JER 38:6 'Malchiah ben-hammelech' may be a title (royal official) or 'the king's son', and if a son it does not say of which king. The text does not establish him as Zedekiah's son.

codex_why: The Merarite named here is Kish represented by kish-son-of-abdi, not the separately recorded Kishi.
judge_why: Kishi son of Abdi is a Merarite by 1CH 6:44 ('sons of Merari ... Kishi son of Abdi'), and 2CH 29:12 likewise has 'of the sons of Merari, Kish son of Abdi'. The descent is true.

codex_why: The Hebrew explicitly includes Isshiah among the men designated Korahites.

codex_why: The verse identifies Heber with the descendants of Hobab but does not mention Reuel or state descent from him.
judge_why: JDG 4:11 places Heber 'of the children of Hobab (מבני חבב)', and Hobab is Reuel's son (NUM 10:29). Heber is therefore Reuel's descendant.

codex_why: The Hebrew explicitly says Mordecai took Hadassah (Esther) as his daughter after her parents died.
judge_why: EST 2:7: Esther is Mordecai's 'uncle's daughter' (בת־דדו), already recorded as cousin, whom he 'took for his own daughter' (לקחה ... לו לבת). An adoption, not daughter-of.
